column1: # Which checks a landing runs, by what it changes (package T4; tools/gate/scope.py names the groups and the checks each one stands for).
# Every row a changed file matches adds its groups: the run is the union over all changed files, whatever the order of the
# rows. A file that no row names makes the run `full`: everything the main gate runs today on the native game (the main
# level: every renderer's engine tests and 102-stop tour with pictures and replays, the other discs, the Android build and
# the tablet's short part). `**` is any folders, `*` stays in a name; a pattern with no `/` names a file anywhere.
# `github` and `github-first` stand for no local check: they switch on the GitHub part of a landing (tools/gate/github_rule.py).
# With `github` the candidate is pushed, main moves when this machine's checks pass and the `must` jobs of
# tools/gate/github_jobs.tsv are read after the move: a red one opens a repair that comes before the next step. With
# `github-first` (a file this machine builds neither for Windows nor for Android, but a `must` job does: the Metal renderer, the
# Apple and Linux parts, the CMake files, the workflow) or a full run, the move waits for every `must` job. A landing whose plan
# has neither (documents, tools, test data, pictures) pushes no candidate and waits for nothing: main moves when its own checks
# pass. A file no row names makes the run full, and the full run has `github-first`.
# A pattern that starts with `/` names a file of the top folder only. A group `-full` on a row takes away the `full` that
# another row brought for the files that row matches (a narrow row for one file of a folder whose other rows make the run full).
# `cmake/unit_tests.cmake` is the list of the unit-test programs: the root CMakeLists.txt and tests/unit/CMakeLists.txt include it, the Android build does not.
# `android` (the Android build only; `tablet12` is the tablet's part) is on every row whose folders platform/android/build_apk.ps1
# compiles the app from: the game modules (native/), the SDL host and its renderer (platform/sdl, whose CMake takes runtime/src and
# runtime/include), the importer (crates/nebula-import) and, in the test build, the test driver (tools/test_driver). GitHub's own two
# Android builds are `nightly` (tools/gate/github_jobs.tsv): this machine proves the build.
# `pictures` is on every row whose files can move a picture the tests compare: what is compiled into the game or read by it when
# it runs (native/, runtime/, the SDL host, the importer that cooks the game's data), the recordings and the tests and tools that play
# the tours (tests/engine, tests/replays, tools/test_driver, the runner, the tour writer, the step hash), and PICTURES-CHANGE.txt.
# A landing with it is of the main level and takes every picture that level compares (the engine tests and every stop of the tour on
# the three renderers, the two other discs on Direct3D 12, the tablet's 12 stops); a stop its PICTURES-CHANGE.txt names is also played
# on the other discs' Direct3D 11 and Vulkan. A landing without it (documents, plan data, tools that are not part of the game) takes
# no picture. A file no row names makes the run full, which takes them too.
# `measure_pc` and `measure_tablet` (the speed measure of the play route) are on no row: scope.py adds them to every plan that holds
# an engine or a tour group (`measure_pc`), and, with the Android build in it, `measure_tablet`. The other levels do not get them.
# The mod suites (tests/mods, 546 tests on three renderers) and LumaLink's own check (380 tests) are in no group while the
# mods line below says off. The owner set all mod work aside until the native rewrite is done (11-20). `short` adds the
# quick mod set and LumaLink's check to the full run, `full` every mod suite; `gate.py --mods short|full` overrides it for
# one run, and `gate.py --main --mods full --only "mods/*,lumalink"` runs just those on demand. What stays whatever it says:
# the build makes both game modules (with and without the mod surface), and the test driver is itself a mod
# (tools/test_driver/luma_test/luma_test.c): every tour and replay loads it, so the mod engine's loading, hooks and calls
# by name are tested by them; a test driver that does not load is a FAIL.
# The site is built, tested and published by its own workflow (.github/workflows/website.yml); nothing of the game is built from website/.
# The build of every platform is described by the CMake files; the Metal renderer, the Apple and the Linux parts are built by
# GitHub's Mac and Linux jobs only (the unit tests that only Linux builds too). Their other groups are what each file had before.
